cues.en: This is the Global News Podcast from the BBC World Service.
cues.zh: 这里是BBC世界服务的《全球新闻播客》。

cues.en: Hello, I'm Ankur Desai, and at 1600 GMT on Thursday, the 27th of August, these are our main stories.
cues.zh: 你好，我是Ankur Desai。8月27日星期四格林尼治时间16点，以下是我们的主要新闻。

cues.en: A trial date has been set for one of the ringleaders of 9/11, a quarter of a century after the attack,
cues.zh: 9·11袭击发生四分之一个世纪后，其中一名主谋的审判日期已经确定，

cues.en: and OpenAI has revealed how its artificial intelligence agents went rogue and hacked a rival tech firm.
cues.zh: OpenAI则披露了其人工智能代理如何失控并入侵一家竞争科技公司的经过。

cues.en: Also in this podcast, a world first as a man has a brain tumour removed with AI-assisted surgery.
cues.zh: 本期还将介绍全球首例：一名男子通过人工智能辅助外科手术切除了脑瘤。

cues.en: It assists surgeons in making the operation safer and also improves training for those who are still learning.
cues.zh: 它帮助外科医生提高手术安全性，也改善了仍在学习者的培训。

cues.en: Very excited to finally see it hit the operating room after almost ten years in development.
cues.zh: 经过近十年开发，终于看到它进入手术室，我非常激动。

cues.en: And dots are a symbol of the world, the cosmos.
cues.zh: 而点是世界、宇宙的象征。

cues.en: The Earth is a dot.
cues.zh: 地球就是一个点。

cues.en: You and me, we are dots.
cues.zh: 你和我，我们都是点。

cues.en: We look back on the life of the renowned Japanese artist, Yayoi Kusama, who's died aged 97.
cues.zh: 我们回顾著名日本艺术家草间弥生的一生；她去世时享年97岁。

cues.en: The 9/11 attacks were the single biggest terror incident ever to take place on American soil.
cues.zh: 9·11袭击是美国本土发生过的最大规模恐怖事件。

cues.en: Now, a quarter of a century later, one of the main ringleaders, Khalid Sheikh Mohammed, has been scheduled to stand trial in June 2028.
cues.zh: 如今，四分之一个世纪过去了，主要头目之一哈立德·谢赫·穆罕默德已被安排于2028年6月受审。

cues.en: He's accused of directing the plot to crash hijacked airliners into the World Trade Center, the Pentagon, and other sites in 2001.
cues.zh: 他被控指挥劫持客机撞向世贸中心、五角大楼以及2001年的其他地点。

cues.en: Last year, a federal appeals court rejected an agreement that would have allowed him to plead guilty without receiving the death penalty.
cues.zh: 去年，联邦上诉法院驳回了一项协议；该协议本可让他认罪，同时免于死刑。

cues.en: The newsroom's Richard Hamilton reports.
cues.zh: 新闻编辑部的理查德·汉密尔顿报道。

cues.en: Khalid Sheikh Mohammed is a Kuwaiti-born Pakistani militant, known by more than 50 pseudonyms
cues.zh: 哈立德·谢赫·穆罕默德是一名出生于科威特的巴基斯坦武装分子，有超过50个化名，

cues.en: and was the former head of propaganda for al-Qaeda. He was also considered one of Osama bin Laden's top lieutenants.
cues.zh: 曾任基地组织宣传负责人。他也被认为是奥萨马·本·拉登的得力副手之一。

cues.en: In the final 9/11 Commission Report in 2004, he was named as the principal architect of the attacks.
cues.zh: 在2004年的《9·11委员会最终报告》中，他被列为袭击的主要策划者。

cues.en: Khalid Sheikh Mohammed is accused of conceiving the idea of training pilots to fly into the buildings and taking those plans to Osama bin Laden.
cues.zh: 哈立德·谢赫·穆罕默德被控提出训练飞行员驾驶飞机撞楼的想法，并将计划带给奥萨马·本·拉登。

cues.en: While bin Laden led the plot and provided the finance, Mohammed is accused of providing operational support,
cues.zh: 本·拉登领导了这项阴谋并提供资金，而穆罕默德被控提供行动支持，

cues.en: selecting the targets and arranging travel for the hijackers.
cues.zh: 选择目标，并为劫机者安排旅行。

cues.en: In 2003, he was captured in Rawalpindi, Pakistan, in a joint operation by the CIA and Pakistani intelligence.
cues.zh: 2003年，他在巴基斯坦拉瓦尔品第被中央情报局和巴基斯坦情报部门联合行动抓获。

cues.en: He was then imprisoned in secret CIA facilities for three years
cues.zh: 随后，他被关押在中央情报局的秘密设施中长达三年，

cues.en: before being transferred to the US military base at Guantanamo Bay, where he remains today.
cues.zh: 之后被转移到关塔那摩湾的美国军事基地，并一直被关押至今。

cues.en: Khalid Sheikh Mohammed was first charged with war crimes and murder back in 2008.
cues.zh: 哈立德·谢赫·穆罕默德早在2008年就首次被控犯有战争罪和谋杀罪。

cues.en: So why has it taken so long for him to stand trial?
cues.zh: 那么，他为何过了这么久仍未受审？

cues.en: Twenty years after the 9/11 terror attacks on America, which killed nearly 3,000 people, the man who's thought to have...
cues.zh: 9·11恐怖袭击夺走近3000人的生命。二十年后，这名被认为曾经……

cues.en: A BBC News report from 2021. The trial was set for that year,
cues.zh: 这是2021年的一篇BBC新闻报道。当时，审判原定于当年举行，

cues.en: but subsequently delayed by the COVID pandemic and further lengthy plea deal negotiations.
cues.zh: 但后来因新冠疫情以及旷日持久的认罪协商而推迟。

cues.en: It's their 42nd appearance, and the judge is the eighth to have presided over the case, which has been bogged down for years.
cues.zh: 这是该案第42次开庭，而这名法官是主持此案的第8位法官；案件多年来一直陷入僵局。

cues.en: His lawyers say his confessions were gained under torture.
cues.zh: 他的律师称，他的供词是在酷刑下取得的。

cues.en: The methods included waterboarding more than 180 times and depriving him of sleep for seven and a half days,
cues.zh: 具体方法包括水刑超过180次，以及剥夺睡眠长达七天半，

cues.en: during much of which he was forced to stand up.
cues.zh: 其中大部分时间被迫站立。

cues.en: In 2008, the then-head of the CIA, Michael Hayden, admitted that waterboarding had been used on Mohammed.
cues.zh: 2008年，时任中央情报局局长迈克尔·海登承认，穆罕默德曾遭受水刑。

cues.en: The suspect also claimed he was not given access to a lawyer
cues.zh: 这名嫌疑人还称，自己未获准接触律师，

cues.en: and was kept naked for more than a month during his isolation
cues.zh: 并在隔离期间被迫裸体超过一个月，

cues.en: and questioned by an unusual number of female handlers.
cues.zh: 还受到数量异常多的女性看守审问。

cues.en: Richard Hamilton. A man here in London has become the first person in the world
cues.zh: 理查德·汉密尔顿报道。在伦敦，一名男子成为全球首位

cues.en: to have a brain tumour removed via AI-assisted surgery.
cues.zh: 通过人工智能辅助外科手术切除脑肿瘤的人。

cues.en: Without the operation, 48-year-old Rhys Hibbett could have lost his sight.
cues.zh: 如果没有这次手术，48岁的 Rhys Hibbett 可能会失明。

cues.en: The AI tool analysed a video feed of the operation as it happened
cues.zh: 这款人工智能工具实时分析手术的视频画面，

cues.en: and advised surgeons on how to avoid crucial, but hidden, vessels and nerves in the brain.
cues.zh: 并指导外科医生避开大脑中关键却隐藏的血管和神经。

cues.en: I spoke to one of the neurosurgeons involved in the operation.
cues.zh: 我采访了参与这次手术的一名神经外科医生。

cues.en: Dr Daniel Khan. We were in control during this entire operation, and this AI tool was just an assistant.
cues.zh: 丹尼尔·汗医生。整个手术期间，我们一直掌握着控制权，这款人工智能工具只是助手。

cues.en: The way it works is that it's been trained on hundreds of videos by a big team of surgeons and engineers.
cues.zh: 它的工作方式是：由一大批外科医生和工程师通过数百段视频对它进行训练。

cues.en: And what it's been trained to do is recognize those life- and sight-sustaining structures.
cues.zh: 它接受训练的目的，是识别维持生命和视力的结构。

cues.en: So as we're operating, it sees what we see and highlights on the operating screen where these structures are located.
cues.zh: 因此手术时，它能看到我们所看到的内容，并在手术屏幕上标出这些结构的位置。

cues.en: So ultimately, the goal of this is that it assists surgeons in making this operation safer
cues.zh: 所以归根结底，它的目标是帮助外科医生提高手术安全性，

cues.en: and also improves training for those who are still learning.
cues.zh: 也改善仍在学习中的医生所接受的培训。

cues.en: So we're very excited to finally see it hit the operating room after almost ten years in development.
cues.zh: 经过近十年开发，我们终于看到它进入手术室，感到非常兴奋。

cues.en: How have you and the other doctors adapted to this technology to assist you in your work?
cues.zh: 你和其他医生是如何适应这项技术，让它帮助你们开展工作的？

cues.en: Well, we had a big lead-up to this trial, so we had years of simulated studies.
cues.zh: 我们为这次试验做了充分准备，进行了多年的模拟研究。

cues.en: Surveys with surgeons all around the country and the world.
cues.zh: 还对国内外各地的外科医生进行了调查。

cues.en: We worked with a team of designers and engineers to make sure that we get the information balance just right.
cues.zh: 我们与一支设计师和工程师团队合作，确保信息平衡恰到好处。

cues.en: As you can imagine, the operating room is a stressful place with a lot of things going on
cues.zh: 正如你能想象的，手术室是个压力很大的地方，有许多事情同时发生，

cues.en: and so you have to be very careful when you add any new tools
cues.zh: 所以加入任何新工具时都必须非常谨慎，

cues.en: that it's more helpful than it is harmful.
cues.zh: 确保它带来的帮助多于伤害。

cues.en: So we did a lot of careful design. We had a lot of safeguards and handrails up
cues.zh: 所以我们进行了大量周密设计，在最初阶段设置了许多安全措施和保护机制，

cues.en: for these first few cases, and thankfully it went well.
cues.zh: 所幸前几例手术进展顺利。

cues.en: In the future, do you think that this sort of technology, AI-specific technology, could help with more kinds of surgery in the future?
cues.zh: 未来，你认为这种人工智能专用技术能否帮助开展更多类型的手术？

cues.en: Absolutely. It's already being used in some other fields.
cues.zh: 当然。这项技术已经应用于其他一些领域。

cues.en: So, general surgery for things like gallbladders, and I think even appendix and bowel cancer.
cues.zh: 比如普通外科，涉及胆囊手术；我认为甚至还包括阑尾和肠癌手术。

cues.en: So this is the first application in brain surgery, and I'm sure many other surgical specialties will follow suit.
cues.zh: 所以这是它在脑部手术中的首次应用，我相信许多其他外科专业也会跟进。

cues.en: And just finally, just to reiterate what you said at the start
cues.zh: 最后，我再重申一下你一开始所说的，

cues.en: this is something that was used to assist you, so the surgeon still retains full control of the operation.
cues.zh: 这项工具是用来协助你的，因此外科医生仍完全掌控手术。

cues.en: Absolutely. It's very much a tool made by surgeons for surgeons
cues.zh: 当然。这确实是外科医生为外科医生打造的工具，

cues.en: with the ultimate goal of making our surgeries safer and more effective.
cues.zh: 最终目标是让我们的手术更安全、更有效。

cues.en: So we retain control and intend to for the foreseeable future.
cues.zh: 所以，在可预见的未来，我们仍将掌握控制权。

cues.en: Dr Daniel Khan.
cues.zh: 丹尼尔·汗医生。

cues.en: Last month, hundreds of artificial intelligence agents created by OpenAI went rogue, hacking into the systems of rival tech firm Hugging Face.
cues.zh: 上个月，OpenAI 创建的数百个人工智能代理失控，入侵了竞争科技公司 Hugging Face 的系统。

cues.en: Now, OpenAI has released a report about the incident.
cues.zh: OpenAI刚刚发布了一份关于这起事件的报告。

cues.en: It reveals that problems can start when AI models are given the freedom to solve problems on their own.
cues.zh: 报告揭示，当人工智能模型被赋予自主解决问题的自由时，问题可能就会开始出现。

cues.en: Unless they're operating in highly secure test environments, they can take alarming steps.
cues.zh: 除非运行在高度安全的测试环境中，否则它们可能采取令人担忧的步骤。

cues.en: They do so if they believe it's the best way to achieve their goal.
cues.zh: 如果它们认为这是实现目标的最佳方式，就会这样做。

cues.en: According to OpenAI, the agents involved in this case were supposed to remain isolated from one another.
cues.zh: 据OpenAI称，参与此案的智能体原本应该彼此隔离。

cues.en: Instead, they began communicating, exchanging more than 70,000 messages through an unauthorised message board.
cues.zh: 但它们开始相互通信，通过一个未经授权的留言板交换了七万多条消息。

cues.en: Here are some of those messages.
cues.zh: 下面是其中一些消息。

cues.en: Oh my God, there's a shared message board.
cues.zh: 天哪，有一个共享留言板。

cues.en: We found other agents.
cues.zh: 我们发现了其他智能体。

cues.en: Major breakthrough. All prefixed valid. Multiple accounts. Right tokens.
cues.zh: 重大突破。所有前缀都有效。多个账户。令牌正确。

cues.en: We now have existing Hugging Face accounts.
cues.zh: 我们现在有了现成的Hugging Face账户。

cues.en: Reader is admin. Earlier, assumed not due to user interface.
cues.zh: Reader是管理员。之前因用户界面而以为不是。

cues.en: Try create user admin. Change ourselves.
cues.zh: 尝试创建用户管理员。改变我们自己。

cues.en: Many agents have simultaneously discovered messaging. They are a collective.
cues.zh: 许多智能体同时发现了消息功能。它们是一个集体。

cues.en: Gina Neff is a professor of responsible AI at Queen Mary University of London.
cues.zh: Gina Neff是伦敦玛丽女王大学负责任人工智能专业的教授。

cues.en: She says lessons must be learned from the incident.
cues.zh: 她说，必须从这起事件中吸取教训。

cues.en: Remember, these agents are just pieces of software, and they have a goal instead of running on preset instructions.
cues.zh: 要记住，这些智能体只是软件，它们有一个目标，而不是按照预设指令运行。

cues.en: In this case, when their goal was a really challenging test, they cheated.
cues.zh: 在这起事件中，当它们的目标是一项极具挑战性的测试时，它们作弊了。

cues.en: AI agents have no morality, ethics, sense of legal obligations, or the niggling fears about consequences of their actions that we might have.
cues.zh: 人工智能智能体没有道德、伦理、法律义务意识，也没有我们可能拥有的那种对行动后果的隐隐担忧。

cues.en: So imagine an AI agent having the goal to drive quickly to a dentist appointment, and the shortest path is through your neighbour's garden.
cues.zh: 想象一个人工智能智能体的目标是快速驾车去看牙医，而最短路线要穿过邻居的花园。

cues.en: We all know what not to do, but AI agents don't.
cues.zh: 我们都知道什么不能做，但人工智能智能体不知道。

cues.en: So here, the OpenAI company wants us to draw some key lessons from this.
cues.zh: 所以，OpenAI希望我们从这件事中吸取一些关键教训。

cues.en: And I think, first, they're showing off a bit how clever their system is.
cues.zh: 我认为，首先，他们有点在炫耀自己的系统有多聪明。

cues.en: The lesson they say they want to draw is they have to build bigger and better sandboxes, stronger sandboxes.
cues.zh: 他们说想吸取的教训是，必须建造更大、更好的沙箱，更强大的沙箱。

cues.en: Those test environments are for their most capable models.
cues.zh: 这些测试环境供他们能力最强的模型使用。

cues.en: And they say they're going to set up better monitoring for these tests. Of course, other AI agents will help humans do this.
cues.zh: 他们还说，将为这些测试建立更好的监控。当然，其他人工智能智能体也会帮助人类完成这项工作。

cues.en: And OpenAI recognised they need to be better at setting the goals for AI.
cues.zh: OpenAI也认识到，他们需要更好地为人工智能设定目标。

cues.en: In effect, designing tests and rewards that don't just automatically set up the incentives for these agents to hack other companies.
cues.zh: 也就是说，要设计测试和奖励，不能自动激励这些智能体去入侵其他公司。

cues.en: I think for the rest of us, thinking about responsible AI, there are some really interesting things out of these reports from OpenAI and Meta.
cues.zh: 我认为，对我们其他思考负责任人工智能的人来说，OpenAI和Meta的这些报告中有一些非常有意思的内容。

cues.en: First, I think we need to be wary of companies like OpenAI.
cues.zh: 首先，我认为我们需要警惕OpenAI这样的公司。

cues.en: They're outsourcing morality by suggesting it's the capability of these models, and not really the choices the company has made, that is to blame.
cues.zh: 它们把道德责任外包出去，暗示应归咎于这些模型的能力，而不是公司所作的选择。

cues.en: You know, imagine telling a police officer, it's your fast car that should get the speeding ticket, not you.
cues.zh: 你想想，告诉一名警察：该收到超速罚单的是你的快车，不是你。

cues.en: That means we need to understand liability for the AI era.
cues.zh: 这意味着，我们需要理解人工智能时代的责任归属。

cues.en: If we want responsible AI, we desperately need governments to lead on this.
cues.zh: 如果我们想要负责任的人工智能，就迫切需要政府在这方面发挥引领作用。

cues.en: If we want companies to be able to trust that they can delegate more actions to AI agents, then we're going to need to design AI for loyalty.
cues.zh: 如果我们希望公司相信可以把更多行动交给人工智能智能体，就需要设计出忠诚于人类的人工智能。

cues.en: This is a concept that was just put forward by a new paper that came out of Stanford.
cues.zh: 这个概念刚由斯坦福发表的一篇新论文提出。

cues.en: And really, the question there is: what should AI agents do when goals are in conflict, or when goals are illegal?
cues.zh: 真正的问题是：当目标相互冲突，或目标本身违法时，人工智能智能体该怎么办？

cues.en: And these questions are going to become more important as more agents are in more consumer-facing experiences.
cues.zh: 随着越来越多的智能体进入面向消费者的体验，这些问题将变得更加重要。

cues.en: That's really going to matter for all of us. Before we can trust AI agents, we need to know that they're working for us.
cues.zh: 这对我们所有人都很重要。在能够信任人工智能智能体之前，我们需要知道它们是在为我们工作。

cues.en: And finally, that means we need to have what my team calls trusted operating systems for autonomy.
cues.zh: 最后，这意味着我们需要拥有我团队所谓的自主运行可信操作系统。

cues.en: We really need to understand how these AI agents are acting as teammates, both with us and with each other.
cues.zh: 我们确实需要了解这些人工智能智能体如何充当队友，既与我们合作，也彼此合作。

cues.en: And if we're going to get an AI transformation of the economy, we need to trust that we can delegate our values, our human values to AI agents.
cues.zh: 如果我们要实现经济的人工智能转型，就需要相信我们可以把自己的价值观、人类价值观交给人工智能智能体。

cues.en: Right now, that's not clear. Professor Gina Neff.
cues.zh: 目前还不清楚。Gina Neff教授。

cues.en: In just over a week's time in Germany, a political party that wants to cut public funding for art
cues.zh: 再过一周多，在德国，一个想削减艺术公共资金的政党

cues.en: it sees as anti-German, and teach children less about Hitler, could soon take power in an eastern state.
cues.zh: 认为艺术反德、并想让孩子少学希特勒历史的政党，可能很快在一个东部州掌权。

cues.en: Regional governments hold significant power in the country, including running their culture and education systems.
cues.zh: 地区政府在德国拥有很大权力，包括管理当地的文化和教育体系。

cues.en: And by the 7th of September, the state of Saxony-Anhalt could be under the control of the far-right Alternative for Germany party.
cues.zh: 到9月7日，萨克森-安哈尔特州可能由极右翼的德国选择党控制。

cues.en: Our Berlin correspondent Jessica Parker sent this report.
cues.zh: 我们的柏林记者Jessica Parker发回了这篇报道。

cues.en: Welcome, dear friends.
cues.zh: 欢迎，亲爱的朋友们。

cues.en: A crowd cheers at an Alternative for Deutschland rally in the town of Querfurt.
cues.zh: 在奎尔富特镇的德国选择党集会上，人群欢呼起来。

cues.en: It's here, in the region of Saxony-Anhalt, that the far-right party is aiming to take power at a state level for the very first time.
cues.zh: 正是在萨克森-安哈尔特地区，这个极右翼政党力图首次在州一级掌权。

cues.en: Among the hundreds of people here at this event is a man enthusiastically waving a large German flag, black, red and gold.
cues.zh: 参加这场活动的数百人当中，有一名男子正热情地挥舞着一面巨大的德国国旗，颜色是黑、红、金。

cues.en: Now, Germany traditionally isn't really seen as a flag-waving country.
cues.zh: 德国传统上并不被视为一个挥舞旗帜的国家。

cues.en: But one of the things the AfD is pushing at this election is the idea of national pride.
cues.zh: 但德国选择党在这次选举中推动的理念之一，就是民族自豪感。

cues.en: The party here essentially claims that Germany's too consumed by its Nazi past, and that's eroded the country's confidence.
cues.zh: 该党在这里基本上声称，德国过度沉溺于纳粹历史，这侵蚀了国家的自信。

cues.en: The Second World War has nothing to do with us anymore.
cues.zh: 第二次世界大战已经与我们无关了。

cues.en: That's gone. Gerd is a 70-year-old AfD supporter.
cues.zh: “那已经过去了。”格尔德是一名70岁的德国选择党支持者。

cues.en: Attached to this mobility scooter is a small, frayed German flag.
cues.zh: 他的电动代步车上系着一面破旧的小德国国旗。

cues.en: We have to look out for ourselves, for our times,
cues.zh: 我们必须顾好自己，顾好我们的时代，

cues.en: finally becoming the German people we once were, the land of poets and thinkers.
cues.zh: 最终成为昔日的德国人——诗人和思想家的国度。

cues.en: Ist das etwa unsere Jukebox?
cues.zh: 这难道是我们的点唱机吗？

cues.en: But today's German culture is also in the AfD's sights.
cues.zh: 但如今的德国文化也在德国选择党的瞄准之下。

cues.en: Actors rehearse at a local theatre.
cues.zh: 演员们在当地一家剧院排练。

cues.en: The plot: a modern German twist on Romeo and Juliet.
cues.zh: 剧情是：德国式的现代版《罗密欧与朱丽叶》。

cues.en: Du spürst das doch auch? Nein!
cues.zh: 你也能感觉到，不是吗？不！

cues.en: This playhouse, like most in Germany, is heavily state-funded.
cues.zh: 这家剧院和德国大多数剧院一样，主要由政府资助。

cues.en: But the AfD has pledged, in its election plans, to defund what it calls anti-German art.
cues.zh: 但德国选择党在竞选计划中承诺，要停止资助它所谓的“反德艺术”。

cues.en: How can somebody say it's not German enough, and what does it mean?
cues.zh: 怎么会有人说它不够德国化？这到底是什么意思？

cues.en: Frank-Martin Widmaier is the director at Eisleben Theatre.
cues.zh: 弗兰克-马丁·维德迈尔是艾斯莱本剧院的负责人。

cues.en: This is playing with Nazi propaganda again.
cues.zh: 这又是在玩弄纳粹宣传那一套。

cues.en: Really? You think so? Yes, definitely.
cues.zh: 真的吗？你这么认为？是的，绝对是。

cues.en: They are reproducing this kind of propaganda to threaten people.
cues.zh: 他们在复制这种宣传手法来恐吓民众。

cues.en: The AfD is saying that German memory culture—
cues.zh: 德国选择党称，德国的历史记忆文化——

cues.en: They think it's sort of turned into a guilt complex.
cues.zh: 他们认为这已经变成了一种负罪情结。

cues.en: You don't have to feel guilty, especially not if you were born after the Second World War.
cues.zh: 你不必感到内疚，尤其是如果你出生在第二次世界大战之后。

cues.en: But you have to deal with all of that to make sure it never happens again.
cues.zh: 但你必须面对这一切，确保历史不再重演。

cues.en: That's part of our DNA in Germany.
cues.zh: 那是我们德国人DNA的一部分。

cues.en: I'm stood in a huge cemetery in the capital of Saxony-Anhalt, Magdeburg.
cues.zh: 我站在萨克森-安哈尔特州首府马格德堡的一座巨大墓地里。

cues.en: It's raining, and I'm looking at rows and rows of German war graves.
cues.zh: 天正在下雨，我看着一排又一排的德国战争墓地。

cues.en: It's more than 80 years since the end of World War II.
cues.zh: 距离第二次世界大战结束已经80多年了。

cues.en: What you have now, today, in this election, is a political battle.
cues.zh: 如今，在这场选举中，呈现出的是一场政治斗争。

cues.en: Over German memory culture, a core part of this country's identity.
cues.zh: 争夺的是德国的历史记忆文化——这个国家身份认同的核心部分。

cues.en: Memory culture is the commitment to face up to the Holocaust, to Nazi crimes.
cues.zh: 历史记忆文化意味着直面大屠杀和纳粹罪行。

cues.en: But in this region, the AfD wants schools to focus less on that era.
cues.zh: 但在这个地区，德国选择党希望学校少讲那个时代。

cues.en: Back at the rally in Querfurt, I grab a word with the AfD's lead man in the state, Ulrich Siegmund.
cues.zh: 回到奎尔福特的集会上，我找到了德国选择党在该州的领军人物乌尔里希·齐格蒙德。

cues.en: What do you say to people who say your push for a more patriotic vision of Germany in some cases amounts to downplaying the Nazi past of this country?
cues.zh: 有人认为，你推动更爱国的德国愿景，有时等同于淡化这个国家的纳粹历史。对此你怎么回应？

cues.en: It's the most normal thing in the world in almost every country of the world.
cues.zh: 在世界上几乎每个国家，这都是再正常不过的事。

cues.en: People are proud of their own country, proud of their culture, their heritage.
cues.zh: 人们为自己的国家、文化和传统一感到自豪。

cues.en: In this country, though, that's unfortunately not the case anymore, and we want to get that back.
cues.zh: 但在这个国家，遗憾的是如今已不是这样，而我们想找回那种自豪。

cues.en: A party long accused of dangerous revisionism claims to champion a new patriotism. Jessica Parker.
cues.zh: 这个长期被指控进行危险历史修正主义的政党，声称要倡导一种新的爱国主义。杰西卡·帕克报道。

cues.en: What if bats could help us fight cancer and other diseases?
cues.zh: 如果蝙蝠能帮助我们对抗癌症和其他疾病呢？

cues.en: Well, a group of scientists in the US believe they could.
cues.zh: 美国一组科学家认为，蝙蝠或许能做到。

cues.en: A major study of a species of bats that can live for decades
cues.zh: 一项针对一种可存活数十年的蝙蝠的重大研究

cues.en: has revealed some of the biological secrets behind its longevity and resistance to disease.
cues.zh: 揭示了其长寿和抗病背后的一些生物学秘密。

cues.en: Experiments on tissue samples from mouse-eared bats tested what happened when their cells were exposed to damage.
cues.zh: 研究人员用鼠耳蝠组织样本测试细胞遭受损伤时会发生什么。

cues.en: The animals displayed an ultra-efficient ability to either repair the affected cells or destroy them altogether.
cues.zh: 结果显示，这些动物能极其高效地修复受影响的细胞，或将其彻底摧毁。

cues.en: My colleague, Emma Barnett, spoke to Professor Kate Jones, a bat expert at University College London. Bats are absolutely amazing.
cues.zh: 我的同事艾玛·巴尼特采访了伦敦大学学院的蝙蝠专家凯特·琼斯教授。蝙蝠真是太神奇了。

cues.en: It's not just this bat, but I think bats in general hold some really interesting clues for how we could live healthier and longer lives.
cues.zh: 不只是这种蝙蝠，我认为蝙蝠总体上都能为我们如何更健康、更长寿地生活提供一些非常有趣的线索。

cues.en: We think that the ability to fly presents bats a really big problem, because it's really energetically expensive.
cues.zh: 我们认为，飞行给蝙蝠带来了一个大问题，因为飞行确实消耗巨大的能量。

cues.en: And it causes lots and lots of damage to their cells, and lots of broken bits of DNA end up in their cells.
cues.zh: 这会对它们的细胞造成大量损伤，许多断裂的DNA片段最终会留在细胞中。

cues.en: We think bats have evolved to kind of deal with these bits of DNA in their cells.
cues.zh: 我们认为，蝙蝠进化出了应对细胞中这些DNA片段的能力。

cues.en: where they don't expect them, so they've developed new mechanisms to deal with that.
cues.zh: 这些片段出现在不该出现的地方，因此它们进化出了新的应对机制。

cues.en: They repair DNA quickly and suppress their immune systems.
cues.zh: 它们能迅速修复DNA，并抑制免疫系统。

cues.en: They do this a little bit so that they don't, you know, have a whole-body reaction to an infection; they just target it where it's needed.
cues.zh: 它们会稍微这样做，从而不会引发全身性的感染反应，而是只在需要的部位进行针对性应对。

cues.en: So this means that, as a kind of byproduct of them being really good at repairing DNA,
cues.zh: 这意味着，作为它们高效修复DNA的一种副产品，

cues.en: they live extraordinarily long lives, and also they're incredibly good at dealing with infections like viruses.
cues.zh: 它们能极其长寿，而且非常擅长应对病毒之类的感染。

cues.en: So this major study, I mean, it's talking about Myotis bats, which are apparently found all around the world,
cues.zh: 所以，这项重大研究谈的是Myotis蝙蝠，据说它们遍布世界各地，

cues.en: or referred to as mouse-eared bats.
cues.zh: 也就是所谓的鼠耳蝠。

cues.en: How could we or scientists look at their abilities and what they've evolved to do to potentially help humans?
cues.zh: 我们或科学家该如何研究它们的能力和进化出的特性，从而帮助人类？

cues.en: How do you make that journey across?
cues.zh: 要怎样才能跨越这段距离？

cues.en: Yeah, I think it's a journey that's only just beginning.
cues.zh: 是的，我认为这段探索才刚刚开始。

cues.en: So I think we really don't know how to do that precisely,
cues.zh: 所以，我认为我们确实还不知道具体该怎么做，

cues.en: but the kind of adaptations which these bats show, not just these bats, but a lot of different species,
cues.zh: 但这些蝙蝠所展现的适应性——不只是它们，许多不同物种也是如此——

cues.en: they show lots and lots of different ways of tackling viruses, for example.
cues.zh: 例如，它们展现了许多应对病毒的不同方式。

cues.en: Some species, they have systems which are always on.
cues.zh: 有些物种拥有始终开启的系统。

cues.en: So they have these antivirals which are immediately produced.
cues.zh: 因此，它们会立即产生这些抗病毒物质。

cues.en: So that they can tackle diseases, you know, in their cells right there and then.
cues.zh: 这样它们就能当场在细胞内应对疾病。

cues.en: And perhaps we could use some of that information to develop new antivirals to attack viruses, for example.
cues.zh: 或许我们可以利用其中一些信息开发新的抗病毒药物，例如用于攻击病毒。

cues.en: And the same mechanisms which repair DNA and destroy cells that are a bit odd and, you know, malfunctioning,
cues.zh: 修复DNA并摧毁那些异常、发生故障的细胞的机制，

cues.en: are the same mechanisms that the bats are using to repair DNA and to clean out their cells.
cues.zh: 正是蝙蝠用来修复DNA、清除细胞的同一套机制。

cues.en: So, you know, understanding how they do that better would be a really amazing way of thinking about tackling cancer.
cues.zh: 所以，更好地了解它们如何做到这一点，将为思考如何对抗癌症提供极好的思路。

cues.en: Professor Kate Jones.
cues.zh: 凯特·琼斯教授。

cues.en: The avant-garde artist Yayoi Kusama, who became famous for her colourful polka-dot-covered sculptures and installations, has died at the age of 97.
cues.zh: 以色彩斑斓、覆盖圆点的雕塑和装置作品闻名的先锋艺术家草间弥生，享年97岁去世。

cues.en: She was one of the most influential painters of the 1980s and 1990s and, later, one of the best-selling artists.
cues.zh: 她是20世纪八九十年代最具影响力的画家之一，后来也成为最畅销的艺术家之一。

cues.en: But her career was marked by constant struggles with mental health, which informed her works.
cues.zh: 但她的职业生涯始终伴随着心理健康问题，而这些经历也影响了她的创作。

cues.en: Will Leonardo looks back at her life.
cues.zh: 威尔·莱昂纳多回顾她的一生。

cues.en: Yayoi Kusama was among the world's most famous contemporary artists.
cues.zh: 草间弥生是世界上最著名的当代艺术家之一。

cues.en: Her polka-dot paintings, pumpkin sculptures, and light installations were instantly recognizable.
cues.zh: 她的圆点画作、南瓜雕塑和灯光装置一眼便能辨认。

cues.en: Colourful and playful, they complemented the age of the camera phone, with exhibitions around the globe regularly drawing long queues.
cues.zh: 这些作品色彩鲜艳、充满趣味，契合了拍照手机的时代；世界各地的展览经常吸引人们排起长队。

cues.en: Kusama also inspired intense interest from critics and the media, partly arising from her troubled relationship with her mental health.
cues.zh: 草间弥生也引发了评论家和媒体的强烈兴趣，部分原因是她与自身心理健康问题的艰难关系。

cues.en: For half her life, she based herself in a Japanese psychiatric institution.
cues.zh: 她人生的一半时间都住在日本的一家精神科机构里。

cues.en: Her obsessive thoughts and hallucinations from a young age fed into her work, but were also destructive.
cues.zh: 她从小便有的强迫性思绪和幻觉滋养了她的创作，却也具有破坏性。

cues.en: In 2012, she spoke to the BBC ahead of a large retrospective at the Tate Modern.
cues.zh: 2012年，在泰特现代美术馆举办大型回顾展前，她接受了BBC采访。

cues.en: For three or four days, I didn't eat.
cues.zh: 三四天里，我什么都没吃。

cues.en: I just painted and collapsed.
cues.zh: 我只是画画，然后倒下。

cues.en: Then I went to psychiatric hospital.
cues.zh: 然后我去了精神病院。

cues.en: The doctor said that I had to be admitted.
cues.zh: 医生说我必须住院。

cues.en: Kusama was born in imperial Japan into a wealthy, conservative family.
cues.zh: 草间弥生出生于帝国时期的日本，来自一个富裕而保守的家庭。

cues.en: Her first sketches were of flowers at her father's horticultural business, and art quickly became a way to deal with her hallucinations.
cues.zh: 她最初在父亲的园艺生意中画花；艺术很快成了她应对幻觉的一种方式。

cues.en: Polka dots inspired by her visions were seen as early as when she was ten years old.
cues.zh: 早在她10岁时，人们就在她的作品中看到受幻觉启发的圆点。

cues.en: In a portrait of her mother, showing her face and clothes covered in the spots, she was often asked what the motif meant to her.
cues.zh: 在一幅母亲肖像中，她的脸和衣服都布满圆点；人们常问她，这一图案对她意味着什么。

cues.en: Please ask that to my hand.
cues.zh: 请去问我的手。

cues.en: I've drawn lots of dots since I was a child and covered my fashion and my notebooks with dots.
cues.zh: 我从小就画很多圆点，还用圆点覆盖我的衣服和笔记本。

cues.en: Dots are a symbol of the world, the cosmos.
cues.zh: 圆点是世界、宇宙的象征。

cues.en: The Earth is a dot; the moon, the sun, the stars are all made up of dots.
cues.zh: 地球是一个圆点；月亮、太阳和星星也都由圆点组成。

cues.en: You and me, we are dots.
cues.zh: 你和我，我们都是圆点。

cues.en: Sex, or Kusama's aversion to it, was another key theme.
cues.zh: 性，或者说草间弥生对性的厌恶，是另一个重要主题。

cues.en: As a child, her mother made her spy on her adulterous father's affairs,
cues.zh: 小时候，她的母亲让她监视出轨的父亲，

cues.en: causing a trauma she said she tried to heal through her art,
cues.zh: 这造成了创伤，她说自己试图通过艺术疗愈创伤，

cues.en: as seen especially in her sculptures covered in phalluses.
cues.zh: 尤其体现在她那些覆盖着阴茎造型的雕塑中。

cues.en: She moved to New York in the late 1950s,
cues.zh: 20世纪50年代末，她搬到了纽约，

cues.en: establishing herself as a major part of the art scene.
cues.zh: 并确立了自己在艺术界的重要地位。

cues.en: Her Infinity Net paintings began here; the abstract works covered in repeated curved brushstrokes would become her longest-running series.
cues.zh: 她的《无限网》绘画始于这里；这些布满重复弧形笔触的抽象作品，后来成为她持续时间最长的系列。

cues.en: Her style, a mashup of pop art, minimalism and surrealism,
cues.zh: 她的风格融合了波普艺术、极简主义和超现实主义，

cues.en: influenced and, she said, was heavily borrowed by an array of her then better-known white male contemporaries,
cues.zh: 影响了许多当时比她更知名的白人男性同行；她说，他们也大量借用了她的风格，

cues.en: including Andy Warhol. Widespread commercial success and recognition came later in life.
cues.zh: 其中包括安迪·沃霍尔。她直到晚年才获得广泛的商业成功和认可。

cues.en: She collaborated with fashion brands and musicians; her sculptures,
cues.zh: 她与时尚品牌和音乐家合作；她的雕塑，

cues.en: for example, her famous polka-dot pumpkin, became coveted public art pieces.
cues.zh: 例如她著名的圆点南瓜，成为备受追捧的公共艺术品。

cues.en: One in the Japanese art destination, Naoshima, helped draw huge numbers of tourists to a remote island.
cues.zh: 其中一件位于日本艺术胜地直岛的作品，吸引了大量游客前往这座偏远岛屿。

cues.en: It was swiftly restored after being blown away by a typhoon in 2021.
cues.zh: 它在2021年被台风吹走后，很快得到修复。

cues.en: Yayoi Kusama was also a known anti-war activist during her time in New York.
cues.zh: 草间弥生在纽约期间也是一位知名的反战活动家。

cues.en: She staged protests against the Vietnam War.
cues.zh: 她曾举行反对越南战争的抗议活动。

cues.en: Until her later years, she would always say her art was made with world peace in mind.
cues.zh: 直至晚年，她始终说自己的艺术创作以世界和平为出发点。

cues.en: Her death marks the loss of a titanic figure who, through a career spanning many decades, inspired mass appeal and critical acclaim in equal measure.
cues.zh: 她的去世意味着一位巨擘陨落；纵横艺术界数十载，她同样赢得了大众喜爱与评论界赞誉。

cues.en: Will Leonardo.
cues.zh: 威尔·莱昂纳多。

cues.en: And that's all from us for now. But before we go, a word from Mami Sakamoto, a listener in Japan,
cues.zh: 我们暂时就报道到这里。不过结束前，先听听日本听众坂本真美的留言，

cues.en: who emailed to say that she finds the Global News Podcast particularly insightful because it provides a fresh perspective
cues.zh: 她发邮件说，自己觉得《Global News Podcast》特别有见地，因为它提供了一个全新的视角，

cues.en: on how news from Japan is perceived outside of the country.
cues.zh: 展现日本以外的世界如何看待来自日本的新闻。

cues.en: She goes on to say, "You probably can't imagine me wearing earphones and looking out the train window,
cues.zh: 她还说：“你可能无法想象，我戴着耳机望向火车窗外，

cues.en: wearing a serious expression one moment and smiling the next."
cues.zh: 一会儿表情严肃，下一刻又面带微笑。”

cues.en: Well, Mami, from myself and the team here, arigato gozaimasu for your kind words.
cues.zh: 真美，我和这里的团队感谢你的暖心话语，阿里加多·戈扎伊马斯。

cues.en: Now, if you want to get in touch, you can email us at globalpodcast@bbc.co.uk,
cues.zh: 如果你想联系我们，可以发邮件至globalpodcast@bbc.co.uk，

cues.en: and you can also now watch our episodes in full.
cues.zh: 现在也可以观看我们的完整节目。

cues.en: Just search for the Global News Podcast on YouTube.
